quizzes.title: UAE exit from OPEC: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates has announced that it will leave the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries, known as OPEC, and the wider OPEC+ alliance. The decision is a significant event for the global energy market, because OPEC has long been a central body in the oil trade. Its role is to act as a regulatory authority for the international energy market. Much like a financial institution, OPEC implements production limits to prevent extreme fluctuations in the cost of crude oil. These strategic limits are meant to protect against oversupply, so that prices remain sustainable for both consumers and exporting nations. The organisation adjusts output in response to global conditions, which helps safeguard the economic stability of members who depend on petroleum revenue. OPEC+ extends this cooperation beyond the original membership, bringing OPEC together with other major producers that sit outside the organisation. Because the UAE is a large producer, its departure is seen as a major geopolitical shift. The move could weaken OPEC's influence over the global oil market, and it has drawn wide attention across the energy sector. The organisation's approach aims to minimise volatility and maintain a reliable balance within the global economy. The exit therefore raises questions about how the remaining members will coordinate their output in the years ahead.

questions.q: In which year did the UAE join OPEC?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the UAE joined OPEC in 1967.

questions.q: From which date is the UAE's exit from OPEC and OPEC+ effective?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives 01 May 2026 as the effective date of the exit.

questions.q: The UAE's exit is seen as a sign of which development among oil producers?
options: Consolidation of all producers into one cartel
Fragmentation within oil alliances and growing competition among producers
A complete end to OPEC's production quotas
Joint pricing by the UAE and Saudi Arabia
questions.explanation: The booklet links the exit to fragmentation within oil alliances and growing competition among producers.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The UAE's exit is linked to its expectation of an imminent peak in global oil demand.
Reason (R): The UAE predicts that global oil demand will keep rising sharply for the next decade.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE predicts an imminent peak in demand, which contradicts the claim that demand will keep rising sharply.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Stated use of the UAE's oil revenues
II. Predicted change in global oil demand
III. Long-standing producer tension cited by the UAE
IV. Limit on the UAE's output under OPEC
A. Production quota constraints
B. Tensions with Saudi Arabia over production policy
C. Imminent peak in global oil demand
D. Funding growth in AI and data centres
questions.explanation: The booklet links oil revenues to AI and data centre growth, the predicted demand peak to the peak itself, the tension to Saudi Arabia, and the output limit to production quotas.

questions.q:
Check the statements given below:
I. OPEC uses production quotas to prevent extreme fluctuations in the cost of crude oil.
II. Russia is not a member of OPEC+.
III. The UAE joined OPEC in 1967.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II contradicts its listing of Russia as a key OPEC+ member.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Independent production strategies may increase market volatility.
II. The UAE joined OPEC in 1973.
III. The UAE's exit is seen as a major geopolitical shift.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while statement II gives the wrong year of joining.

quizzes.title: UAE exit from OPEC: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates has announced that it will leave OPEC and the wider OPEC+ grouping. OPEC is a group of oil-producing states that coordinates how much crude its members supply to the world. Much like a financial institution, the organisation adjusts output in response to global conditions. Its aim is to keep supply steady, so that prices remain sustainable for both consumers and the countries that produce oil. Its members depend heavily on the petroleum income that their economies earn, so stability matters to them. The OPEC+ grouping extends this cooperation by bringing OPEC together with major producers from outside the organisation. Taken together, the arrangement covers a large share of the world's crude oil. The UAE is one of the larger producers in the group, and its decision has been described as a major geopolitical shift. The departure could weaken OPEC's influence over the global oil market. The move has drawn wide attention across the energy sector, and it raises questions about how remaining members will plan their supply. The UAE joined the group in 1967, so its membership spanned several decades. The exit takes effect from 01 May 2026. The booklet presents the exit as a development in the international energy market that is still unfolding.

questions.q: What does OPEC primarily use to prevent extreme fluctuations in the cost of crude oil? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says OPEC implements production quotas to prevent extreme fluctuations in crude oil cost.

questions.q: Which country is described as a key member of the OPEC+ alliance? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Russia as a key OPEC+ member.

questions.q: The UAE predicts an imminent peak in what? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE predicts an imminent peak in global oil demand.

questions.q: The UAE's strategic energy shift prepares it for a long-term energy transition to what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE is preparing for a long-term transition to renewables.

questions.q: Independent production strategies may lead to greater what in oil prices? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says independent production strategies may lead to greater price volatility.

questions.q: OPEC's mandate is to protect whose interests by coordinating production policies? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes OPEC's mandate as protecting the interests of oil exporters.

questions.q: In the short term, the UAE aims to maximise which kind of income from oil? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the UAE focuses on maximising short-term oil revenues.

quizzes.title: Habshan-Fujairah pipeline: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates operates a crude oil pipeline that runs across the country. It starts at inland oil fields and carries crude to the coast, giving the UAE an additional route for moving its oil to buyers. The booklet links the pipeline to greater flexibility in the UAE's exports. The UAE's exit from OPEC and OPEC+ has been described as a major geopolitical shift. Because the country is a large oil producer, its supply decisions now sit outside the group's collective framework. The booklet presents a table of suppliers' shares in India's crude imports, which shows how that supply is divided among several producers. India is one of the buyers discussed in the booklet, and the topic sets out how the UAE's exit could affect its energy planning. Taken together, the topic links a national pipeline, a change in the structure of an oil group, and the position of a large importing country. The pipeline and India's stake form a separate part of the booklet's coverage from the discussion of the exit itself. Both parts of the topic concern how oil moves from producers to buyers. The UAE is a major oil producer, and the booklet places its exit within a wider change in how producers coordinate.

questions.q: Which strait does the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline bypass?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

questions.q: Amid disruption risks, what does the pipeline enable the UAE to do?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline boosts UAE export flexibility and enables higher output.

questions.q: India stands to gain from which change in oil prices?
questions.explanation: The booklet says India stands to gain from decreased oil prices.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Heightened market volatility could complicate India's long-term energy budgeting.
Reason (R): India stands to gain when oil prices rise.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says volatility could complicate India's budgeting, but it does not say India gains from rising prices.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Origin of the pipeline's crude oil
II. Effect of lower oil prices on India
III. Effect of the UAE's exit on negotiations
IV. Risk to India's long-term energy planning
A. Lower import costs and eased inflationary pressure
B. Heightened market volatility complicating energy budgeting
C. Inland oil fields of Habshan
D. Direct bilateral negotiations outside traditional cartel restrictions
questions.explanation: The booklet ties the pipeline to the Habshan fields, lower prices to lower import costs, the exit to bilateral negotiations, and volatility to budgeting risk.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below:
I. The Habshan-Fujairah pipeline is located in the UAE.
II. The UAE's exit makes India's de-dollarisation impossible.
III. India stands to gain from decreased oil prices.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II contradicts its view that the exit supports de-dollarisation.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Heightened market volatility could complicate India's long-term energy budgeting.
II. The UAE's exit prevents direct bilateral negotiations.
III. Lower oil prices would increase India's import costs.
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since the exit allows direct bilateral negotiations and lower prices reduce import costs.

quizzes.title: Habshan-Fujairah pipeline: TITA practice
quizzes.passage: The United Arab Emirates has built a crude oil pipeline that runs across the country. It starts at inland fields and carries crude to a port on the Gulf of Oman. The pipeline is part of the UAE's wider approach to moving its oil to buyers. The UAE has announced that it will leave OPEC and OPEC+, and the decision has been called a major geopolitical shift. The exit could weaken OPEC's influence over the global oil market. The UAE is a large oil producer whose production decisions are now its own. India is among the buyers discussed in the booklet. The booklet shows India's crude imports across several suppliers, with each supplier holding a different share. It also discusses how changes in the oil market could shape India's energy planning in the coming period. Taken together, the topic connects a pipeline, a change among producers and the energy position of a large importing country. Each part of the topic is discussed separately in the booklet. The exit takes effect from 01 May 2026. The UAE holds large oil reserves, which the booklet notes in its discussion of the country's position. The booklet presents the material in short sections, starting with the exit and moving to its wider effects.

questions.q: Which inland oil fields does the pipeline connect to the coast? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline connects the inland oil fields of Habshan to the coast.

questions.q: Lower oil prices would reduce India's import costs and mitigate which kind of pressures? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says lower prices would mitigate inflationary pressures.

questions.q: The shift allows which type of negotiations outside traditional cartel restrictions? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the shift allows for direct bilateral negotiations.

questions.q: The pipeline boosts the UAE's export what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline boosts UAE export flexibility.

questions.q: What else does the pipeline enable the UAE to achieve, amid disruption risks? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline enables higher output amid disruption risks.

questions.q: Heightened market what could complicate India's long-term energy budgeting? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says heightened market volatility could complicate India's long-term energy budgeting.

questions.q: Which strait does the pipeline bypass? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the pipeline bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.
